config.source:
-- Dataset: kpi_headline
-- One row of whole-book headline numbers. Feeds the counter tiles on both dashboard pages.
--
-- Why one pre-computed row: ratios (specialty share, PMPM, claims per 1,000) must be "sum of the
-- numerator ÷ sum of the denominator". Averaging monthly or per-plan ratios in a widget would give the
-- wrong answer, so the ratios are computed here in SQL, once, and the tiles just display them.
-- Money is shown in $M (rounded) so the tiles need no number formatting.

WITH spend AS (
  SELECT
    sum(claim_count)                                                AS claims,
    sum(gross_cost)                                                 AS gross_cost,
    sum(plan_paid)                                                  AS plan_paid,
    sum(CASE WHEN specialty_flag = 'Y' THEN gross_cost  ELSE 0 END) AS specialty_gross_cost,
    sum(CASE WHEN specialty_flag = 'Y' THEN claim_count ELSE 0 END) AS specialty_claims
  FROM portfolio.gold.drug_spend_monthly
),
util AS (  -- rates use only members we can place in a plan (UNKNOWN_MEMBER has no denominator)
  SELECT
    sum(member_months)                                                      AS member_months,
    sum(CASE WHEN plan_id <> 'UNKNOWN_MEMBER' THEN claims     END)          AS known_claims,
    sum(CASE WHEN plan_id <> 'UNKNOWN_MEMBER' THEN gross_cost END)          AS known_gross_cost
  FROM portfolio.gold.utilisation
),
rebate AS (
  SELECT
    count(*)                                                AS rebate_claims,
    sum(estimated_rebate)                                   AS estimated_rebate,
    sum(estimated_rebate_if_stacked - estimated_rebate)     AS double_count_avoided
  FROM portfolio.gold.rebate_eligible_claims
),
rejects AS (
  SELECT
    count(*)                                                                    AS rejected_claims,
    sum(CASE WHEN reason_code = 'NDC_NOT_IN_REFERENCE' THEN plan_paid END)      AS unmapped_ndc_plan_paid
  FROM portfolio.silver.claims_rejected
)
SELECT
  s.claims                                                        AS total_claims,
  round(s.gross_cost / 1e6, 1)                                    AS gross_cost_musd,
  round(s.plan_paid  / 1e6, 1)                                    AS plan_paid_musd,
  round(100 * s.specialty_gross_cost / s.gross_cost, 1)           AS specialty_pct_of_spend,
  round(100 * s.specialty_claims / s.claims, 1)                   AS specialty_pct_of_claims,
  u.member_months,
  round(u.known_claims * 12000.0 / u.member_months, 0)            AS claims_per_1000_per_year,
  round(u.known_gross_cost / u.member_months, 2)                  AS gross_cost_pmpm,
  r.rebate_claims,
  round(r.estimated_rebate / 1e6, 2)                              AS estimated_rebate_musd,
  round(r.double_count_avoided / 1e6, 2)                          AS double_count_avoided_musd,
  j.rejected_claims,
  round(j.unmapped_ndc_plan_paid / 1e6, 2)                        AS unmapped_ndc_plan_paid_musd
FROM spend s
CROSS JOIN util u
CROSS JOIN rebate r
CROSS JOIN rejects j

-- Dataset: spend_monthly
-- gold.drug_spend_monthly with readable labels. Feeds the spend trend and therapeutic class charts,
-- and the page filters (date range, therapeutic class, drug type).
--
-- Only additive measures (counts and dollars) are exposed here, so any widget can safely SUM them
-- across months, drugs or classes. About 11.5k rows: small enough for the 2X-Small warehouse.

SELECT
  fill_month,
  drug_name,
  therapeutic_class,
  CASE specialty_flag     WHEN 'Y' THEN 'Specialty' ELSE 'Traditional' END AS drug_type,
  CASE brand_generic_flag WHEN 'B' THEN 'Brand'     ELSE 'Generic'     END AS brand_generic,
  manufacturer,
  claim_count,
  total_days_supply,
  gross_cost,
  member_copay,
  plan_paid,
  claims_outside_eligibility,
  plan_paid_outside_eligibility
FROM portfolio.gold.drug_spend_monthly

-- Dataset: top_drugs
-- Top 10 drugs by gross cost in the latest fill year, from the gold.top_drugs view.
-- cost_per_claim makes the specialty story obvious: a few hundred claims of a $18k drug outspend
-- ten thousand claims of a $600 drug.

SELECT
  rank_by_spend                                                  AS spend_rank,
  drug_name,
  therapeutic_class,
  CASE specialty_flag     WHEN 'Y' THEN 'Specialty' ELSE 'Traditional' END AS drug_type,
  CASE brand_generic_flag WHEN 'B' THEN 'Brand'     ELSE 'Generic'     END AS brand_generic,
  claims,
  round(gross_cost / 1e6, 2)                                     AS gross_cost_musd,
  round(gross_cost / claims, 0)                                  AS cost_per_claim,
  fill_year
FROM portfolio.gold.top_drugs
WHERE fill_year = (SELECT max(fill_year) FROM portfolio.gold.top_drugs)
  AND rank_by_spend <= 10
ORDER BY spend_rank

config.source:
-- Dataset: utilisation_monthly
-- Whole-book utilisation per month: claims per 1,000 members (annualised) and gross cost PMPM.
--
-- gold.utilisation is month x plan. Rates are re-computed here as sum(numerator) / sum(member_months)
-- for each month, never averaged. Claims for members missing from the member file (UNKNOWN_MEMBER)
-- have no member-months, so they are left out of the rates (but still counted in total_claims).

SELECT
  fill_month,
  sum(member_months)                                                                         AS member_months,
  sum(claims)                                                                                AS total_claims,
  round(sum(CASE WHEN plan_id <> 'UNKNOWN_MEMBER' THEN claims END) * 12000.0
        / sum(member_months), 0)                                                             AS claims_per_1000_per_year,
  round(sum(CASE WHEN plan_id <> 'UNKNOWN_MEMBER' THEN gross_cost END) / sum(member_months), 2) AS gross_cost_pmpm,
  round(sum(days_supply) / sum(claims), 1)                                                   AS avg_days_supply
FROM portfolio.gold.utilisation
GROUP BY fill_month
ORDER BY fill_month

-- Dataset: utilisation_by_plan
-- Whole-period utilisation per plan, for comparing plans side by side.
-- Same rule as utilisation_monthly: ratio of sums, never an average of monthly rates.

SELECT
  plan_id,
  sum(member_months)                                                  AS member_months,
  sum(claims)                                                         AS total_claims,
  round(sum(claims) * 12000.0 / sum(member_months), 0)                AS claims_per_1000_per_year,
  round(sum(gross_cost) / sum(member_months), 2)                      AS gross_cost_pmpm,
  round(100 * sum(specialty_gross_cost) / sum(gross_cost), 1)         AS specialty_pct_of_spend
FROM portfolio.gold.utilisation
WHERE plan_id <> 'UNKNOWN_MEMBER'
GROUP BY plan_id
ORDER BY plan_id

config.source:
-- Dataset: rebates_monthly
-- Estimated rebate per month, by contract level and manufacturer, from gold.rebate_eligible_claims.
-- double_count_avoided = what a naive join that stacked every matching contract would have
-- over-reported. It shows why the one-contract-per-claim precedence rule matters.

SELECT
  fill_month,
  CASE contract_grain WHEN 'NDC' THEN 'NDC-level contract' ELSE 'Class-level contract' END AS contract_level,
  manufacturer,
  therapeutic_class,
  count(*)                                              AS rebate_claims,
  sum(ingredient_cost)                                  AS ingredient_cost,
  sum(estimated_rebate)                                 AS estimated_rebate,
  sum(estimated_rebate_if_stacked - estimated_rebate)   AS double_count_avoided
FROM portfolio.gold.rebate_eligible_claims
GROUP BY ALL

config.source:
-- Dataset: rejected_claims
-- Claim rows silver could not use, by reason. NDC_NOT_IN_REFERENCE is the "rebate leakage" story:
-- claims for real-looking NDCs that are missing from the drug file can't be matched to a rebate
-- contract, so any rebate on them is never invoiced.
-- Reads a silver table on purpose: claims_rejected is already a small, curated exceptions table.

SELECT
  reason_code,
  CASE reason_code
    WHEN 'INVALID_NDC_FORMAT'     THEN 'NDC cannot be parsed to 11 digits'
    WHEN 'NDC_NOT_IN_REFERENCE'   THEN 'Valid NDC, missing from drug file'
    WHEN 'ORPHAN_REVERSAL'        THEN 'Reversal of a claim never received'
    WHEN 'MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD' THEN 'Required field is blank'
    ELSE reason_code
  END                                     AS reason,
  count(*)                                AS rejected_claims,
  round(sum(plan_paid), 2)                AS plan_paid
FROM portfolio.silver.claims_rejected
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY rejected_claims DESC

-- Dataset: dq_latest
-- The 34 data quality checks from the most recent pipeline run (silver.dq_results_latest view).
-- Sorted so anything that is not PASS shows first in the table widget.

SELECT
  check_id,
  category,
  table_name,
  check_name,
  severity,
  status,
  failed_rows,
  total_rows,
  round(failed_pct, 2)    AS failed_pct,
  max_failed_pct          AS tolerance_pct,
  run_id,
  run_ts
FROM portfolio.silver.dq_results_latest
ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'FAIL' THEN 1 WHEN 'WARN' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, check_id

-- Dataset: pipeline_audit_latest
-- Row counts and plan-paid dollars per layer for the most recent pipeline run, landing -> gold.
-- Lets a viewer see that the dashboard's numbers trace back to the files that were received.

SELECT
  CASE layer WHEN 'landing' THEN 1 WHEN 'bronze' THEN 2 WHEN 'silver' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END AS step,
  layer,
  table_name,
  row_count,
  plan_paid,
  note,
  run_id,
  audited_at
FROM portfolio.gold.pipeline_audit
WHERE run_id = (SELECT max_by(run_id, audited_at) FROM portfolio.gold.pipeline_audit)
ORDER BY step, table_name

## Pharmacy Claims Lakehouse

Synthetic PBM claims, Jan 2024 – Dec 2025 · medallion pipeline on Databricks Free Edition · gold layer. Tiles show whole-book totals; the filters apply to the charts.

## Rebates & data trust

Rebate = ingredient cost × contract % (one contract per claim: NDC-level beats class-level). Every number on this dashboard reconciles to silver; data quality checks run on every pipeline run.
